about: This black-and-white line drawing shows a cow looking at two separate doorways, framed by the caption "The illusion... ...of free choice." From above you can see that both entrances lead into the same narrow chute, so whichever one the cow picks, it ends up in the same place. Meme versions label the two doorways with options that look different but turn out to be identical: two political parties, two brands owned by the same company, two ways to do homework you still have to do. It is a cynical joke about choices that are no choice at all.
origin: The cartoon was published by the webcomic Abstruse Goose in 2009 under the title "The Illusion of Free Choice" and became a widely edited image afterward.
usage:
The two boxes sit on the front faces of the left and right walls, each labeling one of the doorways. Fill them with two options that pretend to be different. The punchline is already drawn in: both paths merge into one corridor, so you don't need a third caption.

The joke lands best when the options sound distinct at first but share the same outcome. Two cereal brands from one company, "work from home" versus "work from office" when both mean working, two streaming services showing the same ads, or choosing between two exams that are both on Monday.
